newsitem.title: USA: IBM expanding disk drive manufacturing.
newsitem.headline: IBM expanding disk drive manufacturing.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. said Monday it is expanding disk drive manufacturing to turn its San Jose plant into the world's largest disk platter factory in order to meet increased demand.

The computer giant is adding several manufacturing lines to the 316,000-square-foot plant so it can increase its production of platters -- the key component of hard disk drives -- by "several more million," an IBM spokeswoman said.
IBM will be doing a "significant amount of hiring" for the plant, but the spokeswoman did not have any numbers on how many people the company will hire or on future production capacity.
The expansion will be completed by midyear, IBM said.

The computer company said the move was part of a $1.32 billion expansion of its data storage business, which it began last March with a $500 million investment. Last month, IBM said it would build a new plant in Mulhuddart, Ireland.

"Driven by strong PC sales, as well as high-end storage needs such as network computing, the demand for IBM's innovative hard disk drives has increased dramatically worldwide," Tony Razouk, director of IBM disk manufacturing, said in a statement.
Besides making hard drives for its own computer systems, IBM also sells them to other companies, such as Apple Computer Inc. and Dell Computer Corp.
